bare-string-params.describes: share of parameters declared as a bare string rather than a domain type
bare-string-params.remedy: Introduce a newtype for the concept. Three interchangeable strings in one signature is an argument swap that still compiles and still runs.

broad-lint-silencing.describes: crate-wide allow(clippy::all) or allow(warnings), per 10k lines
broad-lint-silencing.remedy: Replace the blanket allow with the specific lints meant, or fix them. A crate-wide allow also silences everything written after it, including code nobody has typed yet.

crate-type-scatter.describes: crates whose signatures are mostly built from three or more other crates' types
crate-type-scatter.remedy: A crate built mostly from other crates' types, pulled from several of them, usually wants splitting or absorbing. One strong pull is an adapter and perfectly fine.

duplicated-bodies.describes: function bodies that are exact token copies of another, per 10k lines
duplicated-bodies.remedy: Move the shared body somewhere both callers can reach. The copies are listed below; they were found by exact token match, so they were copied rather than merely similar.

env-controlled-spawn.describes: spawn targets chosen by an environment variable, per 10k lines
env-controlled-spawn.remedy: Resolve the program from a known location, or validate it before spawning. As it stands, whoever sets the variable chooses what runs.

exit-in-library.describes: process::exit called from a library crate, per 10k lines
exit-in-library.remedy: Return an error and let the binary decide the exit code. A library that exits takes that decision away from every caller, including a test harness.

oversized-files.describes: files longer than max_lines, per 10k lines — a house standard, not a fact
oversized-files.remedy: Split the file, or raise the standard if this is simply how the project is written: cqx config set oversized-files.max_lines N. Measured across ripgrep, tokio and deno, file length tracks habit rather than quality.

oversized-line-share.describes: share of all lines living in files longer than max_lines
oversized-line-share.remedy: Same standard as oversized-files, measured by weight rather than count: it catches a codebase where most of the code lives in a handful of very large files.

result-string-density.describes: functions returning Result<_, String> instead of a real error type, per 10k lines
result-string-density.remedy: Give the crate an error type and return that. A String error cannot be matched on, so every caller either re-parses the text or swallows it.

shell-invocation.describes: spawning a shell, which turns an argument into a command, per 10k lines
shell-invocation.remedy: Pass the program and its arguments directly rather than through a shell. A shell turns an argument into a command.

undocumented-suppressions.describes: crate-level lint suppressions with no reason given, per 10k lines
undocumented-suppressions.remedy: Add reason = "..." to each suppression. deno documents every one of its crate-level suppressions, which is why theirs read as decisions rather than residue.

unproven-spawn-targets.describes: share of spawn and env targets the extractor could not resolve
unproven-spawn-targets.remedy: Where the target comes from a parameter, the caller is deciding it — hoisting the spawn there makes it knowable. Where it comes from the environment, that is the finding rather than a gap.
